context: The role of IL-15 in T cell survival was examined during chronic CNS coronavirus infection. Similar numbers of virus-specific CD8(+) T cells were retained in the CNS of IL-15(−/−)and wt mice, consistent with loss of IL-2/15 receptor (CD122) expression.
target: IL-15 deficiency also had no affect on IL-7 receptor (CD127) expression, Bcl-2 upregulation, granzyme B expression, or IFN-γ secretion in CNS persisting CD8(+) T cells.
